correctness.rationale: The finite complex is reconstructed from the degree-at-most-two definition. An exhaustive matching has 3663 pairs and critical counts 1 in dimension 0 and 15 in dimension 5; all 37728 Hasse covers are oriented and topologically sorted with no directed cycle. Forman's theorem yields a CW model with one 0-cell and fifteen 5-cells, whose attaching maps are necessarily constant. The independent mod-2 chain calculation has reduced Betti rank 15 only in degree 5 and the Euler characteristic is -14. Risk is implementation error, reduced by full reconstruction, complete DAG verification, and independent chain ranks.

originality.rationale: Direct statement and alias searches found no source giving the homotopy type of M_2(K_{4,4}). Singh's full text gives exact complete-bipartite homotopy formulas only in parameter regions that exclude (4,4,2). Reiner--Roberts gives rational homology for the relevant bounded-degree/chessboard-with-multiplicity class, not the homotopy equivalence. Vega's full text treats other 2-matching families. The closest located exact case is M_2(K_{3,4})≃S^5, which does not imply the balanced case.
residual_risks: An unindexed or differently phrased exact homotopy computation of M_2(K_{4,4}) could exist.
Older rational-homology literature may already encode the rank-15 Betti consequence; the accepted claim is specifically the homotopy type, not novelty of that Betti number.

value.rationale: The case is canonical rather than an arbitrary slice: it is the first balanced K_{n,n} instance at degree bound two beyond K_{3,3}-scale examples and sits immediately below Singh's known balanced sphere M_3(K_{4,4}). The source literature explicitly notes that exact higher-matching homotopy types are difficult. A perfect finite Morse model resolving the homotopy type therefore supplies a reusable benchmark and a concrete boundary case for any prospective balanced-family theory. Risk: a single small case need not extrapolate to larger n, and no such extrapolation is claimed.
